claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens processed around 1700 °C lack a secondary protective phase.
Adding 2–5 mol% silicon to ZrB2 will enable processing below 1700 °C.
Silicon addition will form an in situ silicate or borosilicate secondary phase.
The in situ secondary phase will enhance densification.
The in situ secondary phase will create a self-healing protective oxide scale during high-temperature exposure.
Silicon promotes liquid-phase sintering and enhanced mass transport at lower temperatures.
During high-temperature service, silicon produces a continuous and adherent protective oxide layer.
The protective oxide layer mitigates oxidation.
The protective oxide layer mitigates liquid plating-metal corrosion.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 sintered around 1700 °C will achieve densification and structural integrity comparable to ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 will have greater oxidation resistance than undoped ZrB2 processed both above 2300 °C and around 1700 °C.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 will have greater liquid plating-metal corrosion durability than undoped ZrB2 processed both above 2300 °C and around 1700 °C.
Lower-temperature single-phase ZrB2 specimens can be densified but have limited oxidation resistance.
Lower-temperature single-phase ZrB2 specimens have limited durability in corrosive liquid plating-metal environments.
The proposed behavior is expected for sintering near 1700 °C and oxidation service at 1200–1500 °C in air.
Behavior outside the stated processing and service ranges is not guaranteed.
The phase distribution, uniformity of silicate formation, and long-term stability under cyclic or prolonged exposure remain uncertain.
